page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, it supplies 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU memory-to-core ratio. The processor architecture includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB shared L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. This instance does not include bundled local storage or hardware GPU acceleration, relying on remote block storage solutions and providing a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate modest computational performance relative to modern server baselines. The system registered 1100.49 in single-core and 2931.93 in multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 1990.0 and single-core score of 918.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 163.82 GB/sec for small cached reads, dropping to 20.19 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 18.14 GB/sec for sequential writes. Synthetic database operations scored 1073.82 on PassMark, while in-memory throughput reached 2.87 million Redis SET operations per second. Processing speeds for light language model workloads recorded 243.77 prompt tokens per second and 59.58 generation tokens per second on a 135M parameter model.

The primary resource tradeoff centers on high memory allocation against entry-level compute capability and constrained baseline networking. In qualitative terms, the instance provides cost efficiency for memory-heavy services that do not demand aggressive processing speeds or heavy I/O throughput. The hardware balance is suitable for mid-sized in-memory caching tiers such as Redis, lightweight background ETL pipelines, operational databases with low query complexity, and memory-dependent enterprise middleware.
